turns.prompt: In four short sentences, explain why the sky is blue.
turns.reply:
Perry said

Sunlight contains all colors, but Earth’s atmosphere scatters blue light more strongly than red light.
This scattering sends blue light across the sky in every direction.
We therefore see blue light coming from much of the sky.
At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels farther through the atmosphere, making reds and oranges more visible.

turns.prompt: Now in four short sentences, why sunsets are red.
turns.reply:
Perry said

At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere.
Air scatters away much of the blue and green light.
The remaining light is richer in red and orange wavelengths.
Dust and particles can make these colors appear even more vivid.

turns.prompt: And in four short sentences, why clouds are white.
turns.reply:
Perry said

Cloud droplets scatter all visible colors of sunlight nearly equally.
Those colors combine in our eyes as white light.
Thick clouds can look gray because less sunlight passes through them.
Their brightness also depends on the Sun’s angle and the cloud’s thickness.

turns.prompt: One more: in one sentence, why is grass green?
turns.reply:
Perry said

Grass is green because chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light while reflecting green light.

turns.prompt: In four short sentences, explain why the sea is salty.
turns.reply:
Perry said

Rain and rivers slowly dissolve minerals and salts from rocks on land.
These salts flow into the oceans.
Underwater volcanoes and seafloor vents add more minerals.
Water evaporates, but the dissolved salt remains, making the sea salty.

turns.prompt: In four short sentences, explain why leaves change colour in autumn.
turns.reply:
Perry said

As days shorten and temperatures drop, trees stop making chlorophyll.
The green chlorophyll fades, revealing yellow and orange pigments already in the leaves.
Some trees also produce red and purple pigments.
Eventually, leaves detach and fall to conserve energy during winter.
